purpose: Portable Learning Intelligence + Nova AI core extracted from SolveX (competitive programming) for reuse in SolveX4Schools (school curriculum).

frontend.warning: The Learning Intelligence code is UNTRACKED at this commit. Checking out this SHA yields a repository with no learning intelligence in it. This archive is the only durable copy of the exported state; verify with CHECKSUMS.sha256, not with git.

versions._note: These are cache-invalidation keys. Bump the matching one whenever you change what a projection MEANS, or you will serve numbers that no longer mean what they say. L2-L6 are all rebuildable from learning_events; only the ledger is durable.

knownLimitations: SILENT DEGRADATION: `progressed` and `regressed` (2 of 7 intervention outcomes) are unreachable without per-test pass counts on successive attempts - interventionOutcome.ts:164-174. No error is raised. Emit tests_passed/tests_total, using 1/0 for pass-fail items.

SILENT DEGRADATION: the `thrash` vs `stuck` struggle split collapses without per-test counts (episode.ts:478-499), which disables the unproductive-struggle override that lifts the hint cap for a genuinely stuck learner.

toLearningVerdict (events.ts:423) returns null - meaning 'infrastructure failed, not a learning outcome' - for any status containing 'timeout'. If your grader says 'timeout' for a learner's slow code, that failure is silently discarded.
attestation.ts:114 hard-rejects any token without a string `problem_id`; AttestedSubmission is a judge-submission shape. Keep the HMAC construction, replace the interface.

decisionEngine.ts:206-222 humanize() emits CP prose to learners ('a compile error', 'the running time'). TaskRequest.requires uses pack-verification vocabulary ('degenerate_cases', 'complexity_gate'). Both reach a learner or your catalogue - rewrite early.
verifyAction (interventionMemory.ts:94) returns checkedAt = epoch by design (pure function). SolveX's persist path stamps the real time. If you consume the return value directly, stamp it yourself.

MATURITY: SolveX has no scheduler. The reducer sweep has only ever run from a manual admin button (EpisodeList.tsx:153), so buildLearnerState / decide() and the whole L4-L6 stack have never run continuously against a real backlog. LEARNING_CRON_SECRET exists for a scheduled call that nothing makes yet. If you schedule it, you are the first.
DEAD CODE: hintEffectiveness() in learnerState.ts is exported with 4 tests but has no caller outside its own test file.

BLOCKING/SILENT: ATTEMPT_EVENTS in novaRuntime.ts:214 lists only code-editor events. School interaction events emit none of them, so the escalation guard never lets a learner climb a rung. No error is raised. Fix before hints ship.

Route-layer trust tests do not travel - 3 of 6 trust properties must be re-proven against your own API routes.
7 of 20 Python tests dropped: they pin coach_service.py, which is Codeforces-specific.
Rate limiting in the original keys on client IP. One school behind one NAT gateway is one bucket.
SOLVEX_ADMIN_USER_IDS grants evidence access to EVERY subject, not a class roster.
Attribution coverage in the fixture population is 31/124 = 25%. That is a property of the test data (tiny inputs), not of the model.
starterTemplates.ts ships C++/Python templates. Left unreplaced, boilerplate detection silently under-detects rather than crashing.
Fixtures are synthetic. No percentage computed over them describes a real population.
TaskRequest.difficulty is a direction (easier|same|harder), not a measured level. Per-task difficulty calibration does not exist.
No live LLM is exercised by any test. The directive tests prove what is SENT, never what a model does with it.
designInvariants: Unknown is better than wrong. DIAGNOSE is the DEFAULT action and the most common answer.
An unattributed failure contributes to NOTHING - not a fractional level drop, not a low-confidence misconception.
A misconception needs >=2 distinct episodes before confidence exceeds 0; confidence is capped at 0.95.
mayNameMisconception is false unless a misconception cleared actionable confidence (0.6).
There are four coarse skill levels and NO mastery percentage anywhere.
The NovaDirective sent to a model has NO field for a claim. That absence is the trust boundary.
Directives can only REMOVE capability: effective_help_level is min(), never max().
source_trust is stamped server-side. A browser cannot label its own events trustworthy.
failure_attributed without a valid HMAC signature is DROPPED, not downgraded.
Source code never enters the event payload - hashed into code_blobs, only blob_hash stored.
The read path never writes. Reduction is a scheduled job behind a secret.
Fail open on restrictions, fail closed on claims: a stale projection renders its counts but imposes no cap.
